doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learning English and Chinese characters
summary: English was dropped during the war; she and Brown compare kanji and the tones of Chinese.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: When did you learn English? Did you study English in school?

English was from high school, the very beginning of high school, and, uh, the war started when I was [in] sixth grade, and about a year later, no, maybe two years later, English was taken off from a mandatory class, and it was you could attend the class as a, if you wanted. So, it wasn‟t like a regular class, but you could apply for [it]. Which I did, but I did terrible, I mean I was just…. Language wasn‟t [laughs] my forte.
So when you learned Chinese, of course, kanji is the big difference, and learning all the kanji, so….

Kanji, yes, kanji, some [of them] mean the same, because, after all, it came from China. But most of them are different. Some are the same meaning. But it is a really hard language, the pronunciation is hard [chuckles].
Yeah, that‟s what I mean. It‟s the same thing, but it depends on the tone …
… yeah, different meaning. So it‟s a very hard….
